captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a measuring spoon designed to rest flat on a counter. It features a hemispherical bowl on one end and a long, flat, rectangular handle extending from it. The handle is rounded at both ends and includes a circular hanging hole at the far end, while a small conical support structure is positioned underneath the bowl to keep the spoon stable and level on flat surfaces.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric measuring spoon in OpenSCAD with options for flat-on-counter, nestable, sweep, or ring coupler types. Users should be able to configure the unit system (milliliters, ounces, teaspoons, tablespoons), the capacity size, wall thickness, and custom text labels on the handle.
captions.factory: The code uses conditional blocks based on the 'Type' parameter. For the flat-on-counter spoon (Type 0), a union is created combining a central cube and two end cylinders for the flat handle, a small cylinder as a conical support under the bowl, and a sphere for the outer bowl. A larger cube is used to truncate the top half of the outer sphere. The inner cavity of the bowl is created by differencing an inner sphere, and a final cylinder subtraction creates the hanging hole.
